extracted.intended_audience: attorneys who practice or seek to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; parties subject to reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state court's disciplinary order, describing procedural requirements (notice, opportunity to respond, service), scope and duration of suspension, publication/notification duties, and underlying professional misconduct findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed when a respondent has been disciplined by a duly constituted state authority; the USPTO may impose discipline identical to that imposed by the state unless one or more reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order sought imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the Order of May 1, 2023, of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania. If the respondent files no timely response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose the reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must be given a Notice and Order and an opportunity to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline within the time specified (here, forty (40) days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. provided) and delivered on April 17, 2024. Respondent's failure to file a response supported the determination that there was no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of 'no genuine issue of material fact' upon failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to timely respond to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and proceed to impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and Respondent's suspension ... is the appropriate discipline.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical reciprocal discipline (scope & duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, the USPTO will suspend the respondent from practice before the USPTO in the same manner and for the same duration as the state-imposed discipline (here: suspended for one year and one day from practice in trademark and other non-patent matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order imposed suspension 'for one (1) year and (1) one day' from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO, identical to the Pennsylvania suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of practice affected by reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order specifies the particular areas of USPTO practice affected (e.g., trademark and other non-patent matters) and notes whether patent practice authorization is implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice template states Ms. Keller is suspended from practice before the USPTO in 'trademark and other non-patent matters' and explicitly notes 'Ms. Keller is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public availability obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish the Final Order in the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and give notice of the public discipline as required by the regulations (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires electronic publication at http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov and states disciplinary decisions are available at the OED FOIA Reading Room. It also directs notice consistent with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content and template
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice to be published in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided template must summarize the respondent's identity, authorization to practice, the fact of reciprocal suspension, the regulatory basis (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) here), and a summary of the underlying misconduct/state order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a multi-paragraph template titled 'Notice of Suspension' which gives specific language about the respondent, the nature of the misconduct (accepting upfront fees, failing to complete work, failing to refund, false certification), the Pennsylvania Order date, the rules violated, and a FOIA link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying professional misconduct findings and rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual and ethical bases for discipline include admitted violations of state Rules of Professional Conduct and Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement (specific enumerated rules listed in the Order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ms. Keller admitted to violating Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct: 1.3; 1.4(a)(2), 1.4(a)(3), 1.4(a)(4); 1.5(a); 1.15(e); 1.16(d); 5.5(a); 8.4(b); 8.4(c). She also admitted violations of Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement: 217(a); 217(c)(2); 217(e)(1); 217(j)(1); and 217(j)(4)(i)-(v). The notice explains misconduct examples (accepting upfront fees from clients and failing to complete paid-for work, failing to respond substantively, failing to promptly refund unearned fees, continuing representation during administrative suspension, and false certification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 as the basis for this notification requirement and directs the OED Director to provide such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of a suspended practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (e.g., obligations to clients, trust account handling, notices), as required by the Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically orders that 'Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' The Order's Official Gazette summary references failures to notify clients and to protect clients' interests as part of the misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate of service requirements for the Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be served on the respondent by mail (certified/first-class certified mail, return receipt requested) to addresses of record, and a certificate of service must be included documenting mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The included 'CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE' certifies mailing of the Final Order by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at addresses listed by the disciplinary board and the respondent's last known address with the Virginia State Bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order cites the statutory and regulatory authority under which the discipline is imposed (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24) as the legal basis for reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.' This identifies the proper legal authorities to be used when evaluating or imposing reciprocal discipline.
